PostgreSQL listens on 127.0.0.1:5432. Inspector listens on http://127.0.0.1:8081/.
cd examples/accounting-local-demo cp .env.example .env ./demo.sh In Inspector, click Send streaming and send:
Tell me when an invoice is paid. Keep the watch for 7 days. When the subscription is active, run the printed docker exec update. The seeded unpaid invoice enters the result set. The artifact diffType is Add.

body:
This tutorial runs one curated watch. You will start the demo, ask for paid invoices, mark a seeded invoice paid, and read the JSON artifact. No query authoring is involved. That demo has one published query, and authoring is off.
Prerequisites .NET 8 or newer. Docker, with port 5432 free. AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL set to a model the host can call. Run the demo git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/drasi-project/drasi-sentinel.git cd drasi-sentinel cd examples/accounting-local-demo cp .env.example .env Put the endpoint and model in .env, then start the demo:
./demo.sh The script starts PostgreSQL, Sentinel, and the A2A Inspector. Inspector is at http://127.0.0.1:8081/. The script prints the Agent Card URL. Paste that URL into Inspector.
Open the watch After the card connects, click Send streaming. Send:
Tell me when an invoice is paid. Keep the watch for 7 days. Inspector shows a status update while the task is working, then a message that the subscription is active. Keep that stream open.
Cause one change In another terminal, run the docker exec command the demo printed. It marks the seeded unpaid invoice paid. That row enters the result set.
Inspector then shows an artifact update. The data part has type native_query_diff and diffType Add. data is the row. A text status update is not the change.
What you did not send The message did not include a query id, Cypher, a source name, a filter, or a destination. The host bound the curated paid-invoice query and its reaction. A second watch needs a new task.
Next steps Concepts explains Add, Update, and Delete. Keep the stream open covers reconnect and Last-Event-ID. Ask for current results reads the rows already in the set.

title: Getting started

body:
The host loads one YAML file. Queries and reactions are curated assets. Source connection settings stay in this file. Callers never send them.
service: profile: demo data: data max_ttl: 30d a2a: authentication: mode: anonymous query_authoring: enabled: false queries: - id: overdue-invoices description: Finds open invoices whose due date has passed. examples: - Tell me as soon as an invoice is overdue. cypher: MATCH (invoice:Invoice) RETURN invoice.id AS invoice_id sources: [invoices] reactions: [notify-account] reactions: - id: notify-account service profile is demo, development, or production. Anonymous authentication is valid only when profile is demo. A JWT host sets mode to jwt and supplies issuer, audience, and public_key.
data is the directory for the journal, Drasi indexes, and authored queries. It is relative to the manifest, or absolute. The default is data next to the manifest. Two hosts must not share that directory. Exit one process before starting another against the same files.
max_ttl is the longest lifetime a caller may choose. Omit it, or set none, for no cap. A value is none or a positive integer plus s, m, h, or d.
query_authoring.enabled must be true or false. true requires exactly one reaction. The agent may then create queries against the declared sources. It cannot create sources or choose a destination.
queries and reactions A query has id, description, cypher, sources, and reactions. examples is optional. Those strings are the utterances that select the skill. sources names source ids declared in the same file. reactions names reaction ids. The host binds one of those reactions. The caller does not.
A reaction has an id. The host uses that id when it attaches the watch.
What stays private Source config holds host, port, database, user, and a password reference. Use a Secret reference. Do not put the password in the manifest. The agent does not see connection settings.
Plugin refs, such as source/postgres, belong in plugins. The host installs them on startup.

title: Manifest

body:
Read the Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json once. A skill tagged continuous-query is one watch. Its description says what is watched. Its examples, when present, are utterances that select it.
Send one message Choose a new taskId and messageId. POST message/stream to the JSON-RPC URL on the card. The user text is one example from the chosen skill, or the skill description when it lists no examples. That text is the whole message.
Include a lifetime in that text, or be ready to answer the question on the same task. See Set a lifetime.
Do not send the skill id, a reaction id, Cypher, a source name, a filter, a confirmation code, a destination, or a push URL. The host binds one curated reaction. You do not choose it.
Keep the response open. A later change arrives on this stream as an artifact update. See Keep the stream open.
A second watch is a new task Do not send another watch on a task that already has a subscription. The host starts a new task and keeps the first watch. A mapping answer, such as a stored value the agent asked you to confirm, stays on the task that asked.
To list watches you already opened, POST tasks/list with params {}. Each entry has a task id, a status, and metadata.queryId.

title: Start a watch

body:
The Agent Card is /.well-known/agent-card.json. It advertises JSONRPC, capabilities.streaming: true, and capabilities.pushNotifications: true. POST JSON-RPC 2.0 to the URL of the supportedInterfaces entry whose protocolBinding is JSONRPC. Use Content-Type: application/json and Accept: text/event-stream.
Do not use message/send as the primary call. Use message/stream.
Open a watch { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "1", "method": "message/stream", "params": { "message": { "role": "user", "taskId": "task-1", "messageId": "msg-1", "parts": [ { "mediaType": "text/plain", "text": "Tell me when an invoice is paid. Keep the watch for 7 days." } ] } } } parts is one text part. A part with kind text is also accepted.
Methods Method Use message/stream Send a message and hold the SSE response. tasks/subscribe Reconnect to a task. Set Last-Event-ID to the last id you applied. tasks/list List this caller’s tasks. params is {}. tasks/get Read one task. params.id is the task id. tasks/cancel End that watch. tasks/pushNotificationConfig/set Register one absolute URL for that task. ListTasks, GetTask, CancelTask, and SubscribeToTask are the same operations under their A2A names.
Artifact fields A change is an artifact data part whose type is native_query_diff.
Field Meaning subscriptionId The task’s subscription. queryId The curated or authored query. queryDescription The catalog description. reactionId The reaction the host bound. occurredAt When the host recorded the diff. querySequence The query’s sequence number. diffOrdinal The diff’s position in that result. diffType Add, Update, or Delete. data The row, when present. before, after Present only when the host supplied them. groupingKeys Present when the host supplied them. metadata Present when the host supplied it. A current-results artifact has type current_query_results. It contains taskId, subscriptionId, queryId, queryDescription, and rows.
Null fields are omitted.

body:
Sentinel does not answer a question and stop. A watch stays open until it expires or you cancel it. Later result changes arrive on the same A2A task.
One task, one subscription The opening message selects one curated query. The host binds the reaction already listed for that query. You do not choose the reaction, and you do not send Cypher.
That pair is the task’s only subscription. A second watch is a new task. If you send another watch on a task that already has a subscription, the host starts a new task and keeps the first watch.
A mapping answer stays on the task that asked. A lifetime answer stays there too.
What a diff means Every Drasi query diff is one JSON artifact. Read data.type. A change has type native_query_diff.
diffType Add means the row entered the result set. diffType Update means a row still in the set changed. diffType Delete means the row left the result set. data is the row when the host has it. before and after appear only when the host supplied them. Do not send another request to fill a missing field. queryDescription is the catalog description of that query.
A status update is not a change. Text parts are status.
The stream is the delivery Open the watch with message/stream. Keep the response open for the life of the watch. While the host waits, it writes an SSE comment, : ping, at least every 15 seconds. A comment has no id and is not an event. Do not set a read timeout.
Each event has an id. Keep the last id you applied. If the stream drops, call tasks/subscribe with that id in Last-Event-ID. The host replays events after that id, then waits. Omit the header only to replay from the start.
A push URL is optional, and it belongs to that task only. Streaming remains the primary delivery. The model does not choose the URL.
Lifetime A watch has a lifetime. Say it in the opening message, for example 7d or none. If you do not, the agent asks. Answer on the same task. none means no expiry, unless service.max_ttl sets a cap.
A due watch is detached and marked expired. It does not keep receiving diffs.
Query authoring Some manifests publish a catalog and stop there. If no skill covers the request, the agent says so and does not start a watch.
When service.query_authoring.enabled is true, the agent can build one query against the configured sources and then subscribe. It still cannot create a source, see a password, or choose a destination. The manifest must have exactly one reaction, because the host binds that reaction to the new query.

body:
Sentinel is a governed A2A change-detection agent. A caller describes a supported change. The agent selects one curated query, opens one subscription on one task, and reports later observations on that task.
Where to start Getting started runs the local accounting demo and shows one result diff. Concepts explains a watch, a subscription, and the three diff types. Guides cover starting a watch, keeping the stream, current results, lifetime, and query authoring. Reference lists the manifest fields and the A2A methods a client calls. Examples points at the runnable demos in this repository.

body:
A watch can stay open for hours or days. The HTTP response is the delivery channel. Do not close it because it has been idle.
What an idle stream looks like The host writes an SSE comment at least every 15 seconds:
: ping A comment has no id line and is not an event. Do not treat it as a diff. Do not set a read timeout on this stream. A timeout will drop a healthy watch.
Each real event has an id line and a data line. The id is a decimal sequence. Store the last id you applied.
data is a JSON-RPC result. Read result.kind.
status-update is not a change. artifact-update is an output. A change is a data part whose type is native_query_diff. Reconnect If the stream drops, POST tasks/subscribe with the same task id. Set the Last-Event-ID header to the last id you applied. The host replays events after that id, then waits.
Omit the header only when you want the journal from the start.
Inspector calls this Resume task stream.
Push is optional To receive the same artifact updates without holding the stream, POST tasks/pushNotificationConfig/set with that task id and an absolute http or https URL. You can also set configuration.taskPushNotificationConfig on the opening message/stream.
That URL belongs to that task only. A failed post does not drop the journaled artifact. Streaming remains the primary delivery. The model does not choose the URL.

body:
Current results are not a second watch. Send the request on the task a watch already opened.
Use a new messageId and this text as the only text part:
What are the current results for this task? The output is an artifact update whose data type is current_query_results. It contains taskId, subscriptionId, queryId, queryDescription, and rows.
Do not send a query id, a source name, Cypher, or a filter. The host resolves the task’s subscription.
This artifact does not replace later native_query_diff events. Keep the stream open after you read the rows.

title: Reference

body:
Every watch has a lifetime. Put it in the opening message:
Tell me when an invoice is paid. Keep the watch for 7 days. Accepted tokens are none, or a positive integer plus s, m, h, or d. 7d is seven days. none means the watch does not expire, unless the manifest caps it.
If you leave it out The agent asks how long to keep the watch. Answer on the same task. Do not open a new task for the answer.
The agent asks only after it can start a watch. A request that matches no catalog skill, on a host with authoring off, does not get a lifetime question. The agent says the catalog does not cover it and stops.
The host cap service.max_ttl is the longest lifetime a caller may choose. Omit it, or set none, for no cap. A requested lifetime longer than the cap is rejected.
When a watch is due, the host detaches it and marks it expired. A due authored query is removed only when no live watch still uses it.

title: Set a lifetime

body:
Query authoring is off unless the manifest sets service.query_authoring.enabled to true. That setting requires exactly one reaction. The host binds that reaction to the query the agent commits.
Describe the change If no continuous-query skill matches, send the description as the whole user text on a new task. Do not send Cypher, a source name, a filter, or a destination.
Include the lifetime in that text. The building comfort and curbside demos are hosts that work this way.
The agent reads the configured schema, samples stored values, and probes the query before it opens the watch. A condition you define in the message, with means or as an expression, is part of the query. It is not a stored field the agent should ask you to map.
If the agent asks which stored value a word refers to, answer on the same task. That answer is not a new watch.
What gets stored A committed query is written to data/authored-queries/<id>.yaml. The file has the id, description, Cypher, sources, and joins. The agent does not repeat that Cypher on the task. Later diffs use the same native_query_diff artifact as a curated query.
The agent cannot create a source, insert rows, or see a connection password.
When authoring is off If no catalog query covers the request, the agent says so and stops. It does not invent a query, and it does not ask for a lifetime.

body:
Each example writes its journal, indexes, and authored queries under data/ next to its own sentinel.yaml. Two examples do not share those files.
Set AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL before you start a host.
Accounting has one curated query and authoring off. Building comfort has sources and no queries. The agent builds the watch. Curbside has two database sources and no queries. Invoice overdue is a JWT-protected catalog.
title: Examples

body:
Ask for a change. Read each diff on one task. Sentinel is an A2A agent. You describe a supported change in plain language. It binds one curated query to one durable task and reports later result changes as JSON artifacts.
Get started How a watch works How a watch works A watch is not a one-shot answer. The opening message selects the query. Later changes arrive on the same task.
Describe the change Plain language, plus how long to keep the watch One task, one subscription The host binds the curated query and reaction Read the diffs Each result change is a JSON artifact You do not send a query id, Cypher, a source name, a filter, or a destination. The host already has those. If the manifest enables query authoring, and no curated query covers the request, the agent can build one query against the configured sources and then open the watch.
Delivery is standard A2A JSON-RPC over SSE. Open the watch with message/stream. Reconnect with tasks/subscribe and Last-Event-ID. An idle stream stays open for the life of the watch. While it waits, the host writes an SSE comment at least every 15 seconds. That comment is not an event. Do not set a read timeout.
When to use Sentinel Sentinel fits a caller that needs a governed watch, not a private query string.
A consuming agent should receive each result change, including rows that leave the result set, without polling. The catalog is curated. Callers select a published skill. They do not invent Cypher. The stream may stay open for hours or days. Reconnect from the last event id you applied. Documentation Start with the local accounting demo, then use the contract pages when you write a client.
Getting started Run the accounting demo and see one paid-invoice diff. Concepts What a watch is, and what a diff means. Guides Start a watch, keep the stream, and read current rows. Reference Manifest fields, A2A methods, and artifact fields. Examples Local demos and the JWT-protected catalog.
